claims.text: The local catalog models the World Challenge Secret Super Battle regional third-place source group as one row containing No.3 Trainer at source index 179.
Bulbapedia says No.3 Trainer began as a Japanese tournament Trainer card and later became a third-place prize in the Pokemon World Championships.

Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.3 Trainer iteration was first awarded to the third-place winners of each regional Japanese World Challenge Summer event held between July and August 2000, with the circuit split into Tropical Mega Battle and Secret Super Battle events and retaining the age-limited structure.

Bulbapedia says top-ranking players from Secret Super Battle were eligible to compete in a Best in Japan Deciding Match in late August 2000, while overall winners of Tropical Mega Battle regional events represented Japan in the World Exchange Battle in Hawaii; this dossier does not treat Secret Super Battle regional third place as the Hawaii route.

Pokumon describes World Challenge Summer 2000 as a regional tournament circuit across eight Japanese venues, with the juniors championship known as Tropical Mega Battle and the senior-player counterpart as Secret Super Battle Best in Japan.

Pokumon says the card text distinguished Tropical Mega Battle for players aged 14 or under from Secret Super Battle for players 15+, supporting the senior-track boundary for Secret Super Battle cards.
Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.3 Trainer cards were personalized with the winner's name and regional conference and were Non Holofoil.

Bulbapedia says two base versions of the World Challenge Summer 2000 No.3 Trainer exist, one depicting a male Trainer and the other a female Trainer, with the awarded version depending on the winner's gender.
Bulbapedia says the World Challenge Summer No.3 Trainer major iteration used new artwork by Ken Sugimori, and Pokumon tags Boy SSB No.3 Trainer (World Challenge Summer 2000) with Ken Sugimori.

Bulbapedia describes Ken Sugimori as a friend of Satoshi Tajiri, illustrator of the original Pokemon game artwork, illustrator of TCG cards and merchandise, and the artist who redrew all 151 Generation I Pokemon in watercolor for promotional use.

Pokumon's Secret Super Battle attribute index lists Boy SSB No.3 Trainer and lists Girl SSB No.1 and Girl SSB No.2, but the same index does not list a Girl SSB No.3 entry; this dossier records that as source-surface uncertainty rather than proof that no such object exists.

Pokumon says Secret Super Battle Best in Japan was held at Pokemon Center Tokyo on August 19, 2000 and that winners of that final event received No.1-3 Trainer trophy cards reported to be cosmos holofoil with the winner's photograph printed onto them, but no photos have surfaced to confirm that report.

Pokumon identifies Boy SSB No.3 Trainer as a World Challenge Secret Super Battle 2000 regional third-place prize record, a Japanese unnumbered non-holo Trainer card illustrated by Ken Sugimori, and gives an estimated copy count; this dossier treats that as collector estimate context, not official disclosure.

As judged collector texture, the regional Secret Super Battle No.3 Trainer matters because it preserves senior-track depth: not the winner, not the runner-up, and not the junior Hawaii lane, but still a personalized card for a player who reached the regional podium in the older-player circuit.

narrative.human_title: No.3 Trainer [World Challenge Secret Super Battle regional]: the senior bronze rail
narrative.why_it_matters: The Secret Super Battle No.3 Trainer is the card that makes the tournament map feel real below the headline names. It is the older-player regional third-place route: still a named, personalized trophy, still part of the 2000 World Challenge Summer machine, but not the Hawaii lane and not the later Best in Japan photo trophy. The card asks an agent to preserve the exact route before getting excited about the title. No.3 Trainer is a reusable honor; this one is the senior regional bronze path.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: Use when a card, listing, slab label, auction description, or agent claim says No.3 Trainer, World Challenge, Secret Super Battle, SSB, regional third place, third-place winner, senior division, 15+, personalized name, Best in Japan, photo trophy, female SSB, unlocated Girl SSB No.3, or Tropical Mega Battle.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Treat No.3 Trainer as a reusable trophy-card title. Establish the Secret Super Battle regional third-place route before comparing value, rarity, or historical meaning.
steps: Confirm the card is No.3 Trainer / Ｎｏ.３トレーナー and that the claimed promotion is World Challenge Secret Super Battle regional third-place prize, not Tropical Mega Battle, Secret Super Battle Best in Japan, Challenge Road '99, Lizardon Mega Battle, Kamex Mega Battle, Neo Road, Battle Road, or World Championships.

Check whether the card is the 2000 World Challenge Summer regional Secret Super Battle version: non-holo, personalized with winner name and regional conference, and based on male or female Trainer artwork depending on winner gender.
Keep the age-route split legible: Pokumon describes Tropical Mega Battle as for players aged 14 or under and Secret Super Battle as for players 15+.
Do not treat Secret Super Battle regional third place as the Hawaii representative slot. Bulbapedia assigns the Hawaii / World Exchange Battle path to overall Tropical Mega Battle regional winners.

Separate this regional non-holo card from Secret Super Battle Best in Japan final cards, which Pokumon reports as possible cosmos holofoil photo trophies and explicitly marks as unconfirmed by surfaced photos.

If evaluating a Girl SSB No.3 claim, preserve that Pokumon's Secret Super Battle index lists Boy SSB No.3 but does not surface Girl SSB No.3 beside Girl SSB No.1 and Girl SSB No.2; do not infer official distribution or nonexistence from symmetry alone.
Record Pokumon copy counts only as collector estimates. Do not convert them into official print-run facts.

Before spending or trade gating, require seller-controlled photos of the actual card, including name/conference personalization, front/back, surface, edge, and slab label if graded; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.

narrative.why_it_matters: No.3 Trainer is where the trophy ladder becomes wider and more human. The champion cards are obvious magnets, but this one is a record of someone who still stood on the older-player regional podium in 2000. For an agent, that means the romance is in the boundary work: SSB, not TMB; regional non-holo, not Best in Japan photo trophy; personalized route, not just a famous trophy title.
